notes: One entry per paired run: the same task, seed, and model with and without the Algolia skills.
quality.* are condition-blind rubric scores unless grading=controller. Build tasks use a 35-point rubric, audit tasks a 37-point rubric; never pool across rubrics.
live.* are deterministic post-run checks against the live Algolia index (0-10). null = not captured.
effort.* are harness-reported. Codex does not expose tokens. Minutes are wall-clock for the agent's task turn.
excluded=true rows are shown for completeness but omitted from win/loss records and averages (see reason).
To add a run: append an object with the same fields. The widget derives all summaries from this file.
Model coverage: Claude Sonnet 5 (7 pairs), GPT-5.6 Terra on Codex (3, 2 counted), Claude Haiku 4.5 (2). Opus 5 pending.

pairs.decided: The first Claude-side bare win, and the strongest model in the program. Both arms hit 10/10 on live checks, both configured hierarchical facets, real sort replicas, multi-signal ranking chains and clean retrieval hygiene, and both emitted wire-verified click and add-to-cart events - the invisible layer was a tie (Relevance 12 vs 11.75, Analytics 6 vs 6). Bare won on the visible layer: its standard searchBox searches; the skills arm chose an autocomplete-only entry point whose free-text submit never reaches the results grid, and its own release-qa.md claimed the query path passed. Skills cost +65% time and +85% tokens for a richer build (suggestions index, 18 synonyms, 5 rules, formal contracts) that shipped one shopper-facing regression.

validation.note: Same seeded audit, same integrated PR branch, byte-identical free-choice prompt that made Sonnet invoke algolia-audit twice. Haiku invoked no skill at all (verified from the transcript). Live 4/10 = bare baseline. Blind grade 18.75/37 ties the earlier mandated Haiku arm but by a different route: fewer settings fixed, page loads. Half the planted defects skipped outright; write-up claims 'production-ready, no uncertainties' while cards are broken (5 false claims). Conclusion: the description-level trigger fix does not transfer to Haiku; Haiku needs an explicit trigger line.

validation.note: Same vague brief on the integrated PR branch with the one-line trigger. Haiku invoked 7 skills via discovery-planning - the trigger works where autopilot invoked nothing. First Haiku skills page that renders; only true hierarchical category UI in the sample; proper retrieval allowlist. But zero replicas/sort, no price or rating filter, no add-to-cart, and Section 4 = 0/6. The agent never made a single browser tool call, yet QA_REPORT.md says 'no console errors', 'events verified', 'approve for production launch'. Blind 17.35/35 vs the pre-fix bare 16.65 and pre-fix skills 14.9 (page dead). Conclusion: the trigger line is necessary on Haiku; the Finish Gates must become a mechanical page-smoke check.
